stem: Each node of a singly linked list holds

options.text: Data and a pointer to the next node

explanation: The pointer of the last node is NULL.

stem: Which list lets you move both forwards and backwards?
explanation: Each node also points to the previous node.

stem: In a circular linked list, the last node points back to the first node.
explanation: So the list can be traversed round from any node.
source: general knowledge, following the CSC 341 past papers

stem: According to the course notes, what is the drawback of implementing a stack with a linked list?

options.text: It needs extra memory for pointers
It cannot grow at run time

explanation: Its advantage is that it can grow and shrink at run time.

stem: Which are advantages of a linked list over an array?

options.text: It grows and shrinks at run time
Insertion needs no shifting of elements
Direct access to any element by index
No memory is used for pointers

explanation: Arrays have direct indexing and no pointer overhead.
source: general knowledge, following the CSC 341 past papers

stem: Which one is not a kind of linked list?
explanation: The three kinds are singly, doubly and circular.
